# Intro to Raw Tables

Written by [TheGameAce](https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/TheGameAceReal/mods?gameId=6063)

Most of the files you'll be commonly editing are Datatable files. These files are internally denoted with a "DT" prefix at the start of the file name. Here we'll be going over how to edit those files, excluding Arrays, which will be in a separate guide. This method can also be used to add new entries inside of a DT.

## File + Folder Setup
This part is extremely simple. With PalSchema's main folder open in Visual Studio Code, you'll want to look at the explorer on the left-hand side where you should see all of PalSchema's folders and subsequent files. Navigate to "mods", right click, and select "New Folder...". Name this folder whatever you like. I prefer to use the name of the mod I'm creating for the sake of coherence and organization. In this tutorial I'll just call it TestMod.

Once the folder is created, right click it and create a folder called `raw` inside it. For editing any "raw" datatables, this folder ***must*** be named `raw`.

The last step for setup will be setting up the .json file for editing. For this, simply right click the `raw` folder in explorer, and this time select "New File...". Just like with the mod folder you created, this file can take on any name. **Keep in mind that you need to manually input the .json extension at the end of the file name for it to properly take on .json format.**

## File Formatting
With setup done, we move on to setting up the newly created .json file with proper formatting, and making our first edits. First, open up the .json file if you haven't already. If everything has been handled properly up to this point, things should look about like this (save for names):

![image](https://i.gyazo.com/7bc91b1d4d005097c8e4d80f6c7117ec.png)

Now before we take the next step, pull up FModel so that we can look inside Palworld's container file. If you don't have FModel or haven't set it up yet, refer to the following: [FModel Setup](https://pwmodding.wiki/docs/developers/useful-tools/fmodel).

Once you have FModel up, open up Palworld's main container file. For Gamepass users, this should be called `Pal-WinGDK.utoc`. For Steam users, this should be called `Pal-Windows.pak`. Now that you're in, navigate to the file you want to edit or add to. If you know the file's name, use the search function found under the "Packages" toolbar option at the top of FModel for faster navigation.

For this example, we'll be modifying Lamball's drops. This can be found in the file `DT_PalDropItem.uasset`. After navigating to the file, double click to open it up and use Ctrl + F to bring up the search function, searching `SheepBall` (Lamball's internal name) to find Lamball's drop table. Now let's go back into Visual Studio Code and get to work!

***Tip:*** **Resizing Visual Studio Code and FModel to be side-by-side will help immensely, preventing you from having to go back and forth.**

Back in Visual Studio Code, in the .json file, start by typing a `{` at the beginning of the file. This should automatically create a paired second bracket of the same type (this specific style of brackets are called as "braces"). Hit the "Enter" key to create a new line between the braces with automatic indentation.

In this new space, type in a single quotation mark. Just like with the braces (and other types of brackets), Visual Studio Code should automatically input the other for you, leaving your text cursor right in between them. It's in here that you'll put the name of the file. Keep in mind it should only be the file name and must not include the .uasset extension.

After that step is complete, typing another quotation mark will move your cursor past the already filled in one. Here, you'll need to put in a ":" (colon), a space after that, and then another brace and hit "Enter" one more time.

Things should now be looking like this:

![image](https://i.gyazo.com/e273e2ff52b0283387ed38b58dbf9859.png)

## Editing the File
Here comes the part we want FModel open for. In FModel, if you've successfully found Lamball's entry for drops, you should see this:

![image](https://i.gyazo.com/d5c6edbdcdd28afde0de0accb7bc6b6e.png)

This is what a standard Datatable entry looks like, in this case specifically for Pal drops. This is also what we want to replicate in Visual Studio Code so that PalSchema knows what to alter. But since PalSchema alters only the lines specified, we don't need that whole thing.

To start us off back where we left off in Visual Studio Code, we need the ID of the entry being altered first. Type it out just like you see presented in FModel. **This is case-sensitive, so make sure everything matches properly.**

Here, the entry ID will be `"SheepBall000": {`
Once typed in, hit "Enter" as per usual to create the next line. Your file should now be looking like this:

![image](https://i.gyazo.com/018d09711741ab9e3329abaea413cf30.png)

Under here is where we put in the lines we want to alter for any entry. For this example, we'll add an item to Lamball's drops: Horns. If you look in FModel, you can see all of the data for each drop. Since the line `ItemId3` and it's companion lines contain nothing, we'll add it in here. You can, of course, choose any grouping you'd like, including overriding currently existing ones. This will also be the same method you use for any other standard DataTable changes.

In this specific instance, we need to edit the lines `ItemId3`, `Rate3`, `min3`, and `Max3`. To edit them, simply input them into your .json file under the `SheepBall000` entry in the same way they show up in FModel.

Once finished, it should look something like this: 

![image](https://i.gyazo.com/047de346df16c3707f283f128c337774.png)

This tells PalSchema to alter the entry `SheepBall000` within the file `DT_PalDropItem`, and that in the 3rd drop slot it should drop the `Horn` item (this is based on the item ID) at a rate of 30% of the time, dropping a minimum of 1 when they do drop, with a maximum possibility of 2 dropped at a time.

That's all that's needed! If you were to now save and launch the game, you should find that Lamballs will have horns as an item drop. You can now utilize this process for any DT file and entry as you please!

*If you want to add new entries to a DT file, simply do the same process with a new/custom ID for the entry, and be sure to fill in all the necessary lines for the entry to be properly accepted.*

*In some cases, you may want to delete a row from a table. In that case, simply set the value of an existing row to `null`, and the entry will be deleted.*

**Note: There are some special entries such as Arrays, as mentioned at the start of this guide. Arrays are defined with standard or "square" brackets and may require more specialized modification.**

# FindObject

`FindObject` is a function that finds an object. 

Overload #1 finds by either class name or short object name.

Overload #2 works the same way as `FindObject` in the [UE source](https://docs.unrealengine.com/4.27/en-US/API/Runtime/CoreUObject/UObject/FindObject/).

## Parameters (overload #1)

| # | Type | Information |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | string\|FName\|UClass\|nil | The short name of the object's class or the UClass itself |
| 2 | string\|FName\|nil | The short name of the object itself |
| 3 | EObjectFlags | Any flags that the object cannot have. Uses \| as a seperator |
| 4 | EObjectFlags | Any flags that the object must have. Uses \| as a seperator |

> Param 1 or Param 2 can be nil, but not both.

## Parameters (overload #2)

| # | Type | Information |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | UClass | The class to find |
| 2 | UObject\|UClass | The outer to look inside. If this is null then param 3 should start with a package name |
| 3 | string | The object path to search for an object, relative to param 2 |
| 4 | bool | Whether to require an exact match with the UClass parameter |

## Return Value (overload #1 & #2)

| # | Type | Information |
|---|------|-------------|
| 1 | UObject | The derivative of the UObject |

## Example (overload #1)

```lua
-- SceneComponent instance called TransformComponent0
local Object = FindObject("SceneComponent", "TransformComponent0")
```

```lua
-- FirstPersonCharacter_C instance called FirstPersonCharacter_C_0
local Object = FindObject("FirstPersonCharacter_C", "FirstPersonCharacter_C_0", EObjectFlags.RF_NoFlags, EObjectFlags.RF_ClassDefaultObject)
```

Alternatively, you can use a UClass object:

```lua
local Object = FindObject(SceneComponentClass, "TransformComponent0")
```

## Example (overload #2)

```lua
local Object = FindObject(UClass, World, "Character", true)
```

Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about the Palworld dedicated server client version mismatch issue:

## What the Error Means

Palworld requires the client and server to run the exact same game version. When Pocketpair pushes an update, your Steam client may auto-update while the server is still on the old build (or vice-versa), causing the server to reject the connection with the "incompatible version" message.

## Why It Happens

Palworld's dedicated server does not update itself automatically — your game client does, and that asymmetry is why "incompatible version" exists. Pocketpair pushes a patch, your client picks it up overnight, your server is still on last week's build, and by morning nobody can connect.

## How to Fix It

The solution is straightforward: Get the client and server on the same version. The specific fix depends on which is behind:

- **If the server is outdated:** Update the dedicated server to the latest build by re-running SteamCMD with app_update 2394010 validate and restart.
- **If the client is outdated:** Update your own game in Steam instead.

/**
 * Palworld modding support for Cyrus (PURE, client-safe, data only). Researched 2026-10-08.
 *
 * Two kinds of Palworld "mod" exist, and they behave very differently on a server:
 *  1. Server settings presets: changes to PalWorldSettings.ini (XP rate, capture rate, day length,
 *     death penalty...). Pocketpair supports these on every dedicated server, Windows AND Linux, and
 *     players install nothing. This is the only kind that works on Nxeon's Palworld servers today,
 *     because they run the native Linux server.
 *  2. UE4SS Lua mods, packaged for Pocketpair's official mod loader (Info.json + Scripts/). These run
 *     in the Windows game client (single-player and the host of a co-op world) and on the WINDOWS
 *     dedicated server only. Pocketpair's own docs say server-side mods are Windows-only.
 *
 * Every fact here is cited in `sources`; anything we could not confirm is in `unknowns`.
 */
import type { GameSupport, GameVersionRule } from "./support";

/** The game version Cyrus targets. Palworld clients must match the server's version exactly. */
export const PALWORLD_CURRENT_VERSION = "1.0.5";
/** Released 2026-09-14 (Steam news 2026-09-15). Patch cadence in 1.0: 1 to 4 weeks. */
export const PALWORLD_CURRENT_RELEASED = "2026-09-14";
/**
 * Info.json `MinRevision` Cyrus writes: "the last 5 digits of the version shown in the title".
 * 82182 is the value in Pocketpair's own example package. We have NOT read the 1.0.5 revision off
 * a title screen, so this is an old (safe, permissive) floor, not a tested-on claim. See unknowns.
 */
export const PALWORLD_MIN_REVISION = 82182;
/** Package name of the UE4SS runtime on the official loader; Lua mods list it as a dependency. */
export const PALWORLD_UE4SS_PACKAGE = "UE4SS";
/** Steam app id of the free dedicated server (SteamCMD, anonymous login). */
export const PALWORLD_SERVER_APP_ID = 2394010;

| Terraria TShock | Server commands, permissions, anti-grief, events (R1 to R2) | Anything needing new items or art (impossible server-only) |
| Valheim (BepInEx + Jotunn) | Config and stat changes, clone-and-modify items, recipes, status effects (R1 to R2) | New models and prefabs (Unity editor), new biomes (R3) |
| Rust (Oxide/Carbon) | Kits, teleports, shops, custom UI, anti-cheat tooling (R1 to R2) | New items or models (impossible server-side), monthly-update triage (needs monitoring) |
| Palworld | PalSchema JSON data mods (R2) | UE4SS Lua without an SDK dump, Blueprint LogicMods, cooked assets (R3) |
| Project Zomboid | Item/recipe scripts and small Lua (R2, once B42 golden examples exist) | Models, maps, anything mixing B41 knowledge (R3) |

**Three hard platform facts Cyrus should surface to customers**
1. **Palworld server-side mods are Windows-server only** per community docs quoting the official docs [S: [XGamingServer](https://xgamingserver.com/docs/palworld/mod-installation), [ConnectHosting](https://connecthosting.net/blog/palworld-server-mods-what-works), [gamever.io](https://gamever.io/knowledge-base/server-side-mods-in-palworld-palmodsettingsini-and-the-flag-that-undoes-everything)]. Nxeon's Palworld image is the native Linux server (config path `.../Config/LinuxServer/PalWorldSettings.ini`) [L: `lib/game-control.ts:239`]. Unless that is wrong, most Palworld mods cannot run on Nxeon's Palworld servers today. This must be checked before the Palworld agent's `side` and `reason` strings are written.
2. **tModLoader and TShock cannot be combined**: tModLoader stable (v2026.08.3.0) targets Terraria 1.4.4; TShock 6.2.1 targets Terraria 1.4.5.8 [V: GitHub release APIs]. tModLoader has an active `1.4.5` branch (last commit 2026-10-07) [V], so this will change; Cyrus's version table must treat them as two products.
3. **Rust and Palworld-style "new item" ideas cannot be delivered server-side.** Vanilla Rust clients only show existing prefabs and Facepunch-approved workshop skins [S]. Cyrus should refuse or reframe those requests honestly.

**What Cyrus should add (ranked; details in section 9).**
1. Per-game **version-and-API knowledge packs** generated from the real jars, SDKs and docs, injected only for the target version (the Minecraft "sheets plus failure rules" pattern, generalised). Highest value, medium effort per game.
2. A **structured spec card** (commands, permissions, configs, GUIs, acceptance tests) before code, shared by all games. It also feeds tests.
3. **Golden examples** per game, human-verified and compile-tested, retrieved by nearest match. These double as regression tests.
4. **Multi-file projects with typed file roles** (code, config, data, lang, assets) and diff-based edits.
5. A **verification ladder** per game (static lint, compile, unit tests of pure logic, live smoke test on a throwaway server where the game allows).
6. **Dependency handling** (declared soft-dependencies, compile-only API digests, install-time "requires X" warnings).
7. **Iterative refinement from real server logs**, then multi-step planning for large mods, then companion asset packs (see `RENDERS-AND-TEXTURES.md`).

---

## 2. Method and limits

- Primary sources were fetched with WebFetch or `curl`, plus the GitHub, Thunderstore and Hugging Face APIs, which were reachable. umod.org, pzwiki.net and pzfans.com sit behind Cloudflare challenges; I did not try to bypass them. Where a fact would have come from them, it is tagged [S] and sourced from alternatives (Carbon's MIT-licensed docs repo, a community Build 42 guide, hosting-provider docs).
- `WebFetch` summarises pages with a small model. Facts that mattered were cross-checked against raw files or APIs where possible (release APIs, raw wiki markdown, licence texts). Anything only seen in a summary is tagged [S].
- Dates and version numbers are from release APIs read on 2026-10-08 unless noted.
- Effort figures in section 9 are my estimates for one engineer using AI assistance [I]. They are not measured.

---

## 3. Cross-game patterns

### 3.1 The capability ladder and who can do what

| Rung | Examples | AI today |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Config and data | Stat tweaks, spawn tables, drop rates, recipe edits | R1 when the schema is validated |
| 2 Scripted behaviour | Commands, listeners, timers, simple GUIs | R1 |
| 3 New content | Items, recipes, enchantments, buffs, simple mobs | R1 to R2 |
| 4 New systems | Economy, minigames, quests, custom AI, admin dashboards | R2 |
| 5 Engine-level | IL patching, Harmony patches of game internals, world generators with tuned noise, cooked Unreal/Unity assets | R3 |

### 3.2 Where mods break (all games)

1. **Game or loader update changes an internal name.** Silent failure is worse than a crash: Rust "boots and then quietly misbehaves" after a monthly update [S: [Low.ms schedule](https://low.ms/blog/rust-wipe-schedule-2026), [ConnectHosting](https://connecthosting.net/blog/palworld-server-mods-what-works)].
2. **Client and server mismatch.** Terraria tML, Valheim (when assets are involved) and Zomboid need identical mods on both sides; Rust and Terraria-TShock need nothing on the client; Minecraft plugins need nothing unless a resource pack is wanted.
3. **Threading rules.** Minecraft main thread vs async vs Folia regions; Unreal game thread (UE4SS); Unity main thread (Valheim); Zomboid's client/server Lua split.
4. **Save-data coupling.** Palworld's own docs warn that mods "may cause save-data corruption or crashes" [S]. Valheim persistence depends on `ZNetView` flags [V]. Minecraft PDC data is not copied automatically between holders [V].
5. **Dependency load order.** Zomboid library mods must load before dependents [S]; Valheim needs Jotunn first and then the mod; Paper plugins declare `depend`/`load` in `paper-plugin.yml` [V].

### 3.3 Why the existing non-Minecraft generators need care [L]
The owner's handoff generators (`palworld.ts`, `rust.ts`, `valheim.ts`, `zomboid.ts`) are deterministic templates built with an indentation-aware `code` tag, not model-written code. `palworld.ts` marks 17 API calls as `plausible:`, meaning the name was not confirmed against a game SDK dump (examples: `UPalUtility::SendSystemAnnounce`, `UPalTimeManager` hour accessor, `DT_PalDropItem` columns). Anything generated from unverified names should carry the "Template preview" label until a per-game agent resolves them. The Valheim template already emits xUnit tests for its pure balance maths, a good model for other C# games.

---

## 4. Minecraft: Paper and Purpur

### 4.1 Platform snapshot
- **Paper** is GPL-3.0 [prior research, [V] at the time]; **Purpur** is "a drop-in replacement for Paper servers designed for configurability, new fun and exciting gameplay features, and performance" [V: [Purpur README](https://github.com/PurpurMC/Purpur)]. Purpur plugins use the Paper API, so Cyrus can target Paper and run on both.
- Version lines in Cyrus today: 1.21.1, 1.21.4, 1.21.8, 1.21.11 [L: `MB_VERSIONS`]. Paper and Purpur also publish a 26.x line (Javadocs exist for 26.2) [V: [Paper 26.2 javadocs](https://jd.papermc.io/paper/26.2/org/bukkit/generator/package-use.html), Purpur README branch badge `ver/26.2`]. The service's Java 21 toolchain would need Java 25 for 26.x [prior research].
- **Side**: server-only. Vanilla clients can join. Custom visuals need a server-sent resource pack: `resource-pack` URL, `resource-pack-sha1`, `resource-pack-id`, `require-resource-pack`, a prompt; pack size limit 250 MiB [V: [Minecraft Wiki server.properties](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server.properties)]. Since 1.20.3 a server can stack several packs and remove them individually [S: [Paper Adventure docs](https://docs.papermc.io/adventure/resource-pack/)].
- Hot reload: not safely. Needs a restart or a plugin-manager reload (risky). `/reload` is discouraged [I].

### 4.2 What "advanced" looks like, and how professionals do it

| Capability | Professional technique | Libraries / APIs | AI today |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Custom items** with new looks and behaviour | Stack data components (`item_model`, `custom_model_data`, tool, food, lore, enchantments) on a base item, store identity in PDC, ship a resource pack | Paper Data Component API, PDC, Recipes API [V: [data components](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/data-component-api/), [PDC](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/pdc/), [recipes](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/recipes/)] | R1 for stats and behaviour, R2 when it needs a pack (art is R3) |
| **Custom blocks** | There are no truly new blocks on a vanilla client. Pros emulate with note-block states, tripwire, or display entities, and use Nexo or ItemsAdder to manage packs | Nexo docs, display entities [S: [Nexo FAQ](https://docs.nexomc.com/general-usage/faq/itemmodels-vs.-custommodeldata)] | R2/R3 (mining-speed emulation, drops, anti-dupe are fiddly) |
| **GUIs** | Inventory menus with strict click, drag and shift-click handling; 1.21.6+ Dialog API for forms (text input, sliders, dropdowns, confirm dialogs) | triumph-gui, InvUI (MIT) [prior], Dialog API [V: [dialogs](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/dialogs/)] | R1 simple, R2 complex (dupe edge cases) |
| **Commands** | Brigadier via the lifecycle API, registered in a bootstrapper so datapack functions can see them; Cloud or ACF in older stacks | Paper Command API, Incendo Cloud (MIT) [V: [lifecycle](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/dev/lifecycle/)] | R1 (but see the 4.5 note about Cyrus's current `plugin.yml`-only rule) |

input.content:
# Palworld in Cyrus: readiness (2026-10-08, game-palworld agent)

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-palworld`. Palworld stays `status: "soon"`; going live is the owner's call.

## Verdict first: Linux vs Windows (confirmed from primary sources)

**Confirmed.** Pocketpair's own server guide says server-side mods work only on the **Windows** dedicated server
(https://docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/mod, fetched 2026-10-08). Their mod-loader docs list the
supported platforms as "Windows (Steam)" and "Windows dedicated server" only
(https://github.com/pocketpairjp/PalworldModUploader, `docs/en/01-General.md`). Nxeon's Palworld servers run the
native Linux server (`thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker`; config at `Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/`,
`lib/game-files-roots.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`). So:

| What | Works on Nxeon's Linux servers today? | Players install? |
|---|---|---|
| **Server settings presets** (`PalWorldSettings.ini`: XP, capture, day/night, death penalty, hardcore, base limits, raids...) | **Yes.** Every dedicated server, any OS. | No. Console / Mac / Game Pass players can join too. |
| UE4SS Lua mods via the official loader (`Info.json` + `IsServer` rule) | **No.** Windows dedicated server only. | Only if the mod also changes client-predicted things (movement) or visuals. |
| PalSchema JSON data mods (a UE4SS mod) | **No** (needs UE4SS; Windows only). | Server-side data changes: no. |
| LogicMods / Paks (Blueprint, textures, models, audio) | **No**; also need cooked UE 5.1 packages Cyrus can't produce. | **Yes**, every player. |
| Client-only Lua (overlays, post-process, key-bound abilities in single-player / co-op host) | n/a (runs on the player's Windows PC) | Yes, each player who wants it. |

Ways Lua could reach Nxeon later, both **unverified by Nxeon**: (a) run the Windows server under Wine/Proton in a
separate image (community images exist, e.g. `ripps818/docker-palworld-dedicated-server-wine`); (b) the community
Linux port `XarminaEu/ue4ss-linux` (MIT, verified by its author on Palworld 1.0.1, LD_PRELOAD; hooks need resolved
addresses on stripped binaries, no Blueprint loader, folders must be lowercase `scripts`, and the official loader does
not run there). **Cyrus therefore targets server settings presets first** for Nxeon customers, and labels every Lua mod
"can't be installed on Nxeon servers yet".

## What was built

- `lib/cyrus/games/palworld.ts`: verified `GameSupport` + `knowledge` pack (API sheet from Palworld's published headers
  and the UE4SS docs, 13 failure rules) + `PALWORLD_KINDS` (server-settings / server-lua / both-lua / host-lua / client-lua
  with customer-facing reasons).
- `lib/cyrus/games/palworld.settings.ts`: 70 documented settings with types and safety ranges, a blocked list
  (passwords, ports, RCON/REST, player cap...), `mergeOptionSettings` (pure merge into an existing ini; a partial
  OptionSettings line is NOT a patch), `settingsIntent` (plain words -> changes, zero API cost).
- `lib/cyrus/engine/games/palworld.ts` (generator v2): settings presets; Info.json packages; side-aware main.lua that
  starts on dedicated servers and PCs; all 17 `plausible:` names resolved (fixed or removed, list below); authority
  checks before every state change; data tables found by short name; file access confined to the mod folder.
- `lib/cyrus/games/palworld.validate.ts`: static validator (package format, side rules, Lua block/bracket structure,
  blocked APIs, MOD_DIR file rule, knowledge failure rules, verified-hook list, settings key checks).
- `test/cyrus-game-palworld.test.ts`: generator x validator across every category/model, settings, negative cases.

### The 17 `plausible:` names, resolved
| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `PalUtility:SendSystemAnnounce` | Verified (`PalUtility.h`), called with the world as context, server only |
| `StatusComponent:AddAdditionalEffect` | Does not exist. `StatusComponent:AddStatus(EPalStatusID)` |
| `PalTimeManager:GetCurrentDayTimeHour` | Does not exist. `UPalUtility:GetTimeManager():GetCurrentPalWorldTime_Hour()` + `UPalUtility:IsNight` |
| `PalDamageReactionComponent:ApplyDamageForMP` (pre-hook editing damage) | Does not exist. Post-hit hook on `CallOnActualDamageProcessed_ToAll` + bonus damage |
| `ShooterComponent:GetHasWeapon().ownItemId` | `GetHasWeapon():GetItemId().StaticId` (field is `ownItemID`) |
| `PalBaseCampModel.Transform / AreaRange` | Verified |
| `PalWorkProgress.CurrentWorkAmount / RequiredWorkAmount` | Verified |
| `CharacterParameterComponent:IsOtomo` | Verified |
| `player:GetRidingCharacter` | Does not exist. `UPalUtility:GetRidePal(player)` |
| `CharacterParameterComponent:GetWork` | Verified |
| `IndividualHandle.ID.InstanceId` | Verified |
| `DT_PalDropItem` CharacterID / ItemIdN / RateN | Verified (`FPalDropItemDatabaseRow`) |
| `PalSpawnerStandard.SpawnGroupList` | Not on any native class. Now `DT_PalWildSpawner` rows `LvMin_N/LvMax_N` (verified struct) |
| `PalPlayerState:EnterChat_Receive` | Does not exist. `PalPlayerState:EnterChat(FText)` |
| `AkGameplayStatics:PostEventByName` | Removed: no verified Wwise API; audio is a labelled template preview |
| Monster body `EmissiveColor` material param | Removed (unverifiable); variants keep lucky flag/rank/talents/scale |
| Bare `BeginDeferredActorSpawnFromClass` pal summon | Removed (breaks saves); "summon" effect staggers instead |

Also fixed (real bugs, not tagged): `SetHP` was called on the individual parameter (only the component has it);
`AddItem_ServerInternal` had 3 args (1.0 has 5); the mod never started on a dedicated server (ClientRestart +
IsLocalController only); `FindFirstOf("PalPlayerCharacter")` treated "first player" as "you".

## Readiness checklist (before Palworld can go live)

**Can ship now (owner decision)**
- [ ] Owner: approve **server settings presets** as the first live Palworld mod type in Cyrus.
- [ ] Wire the install: lifecycle agent applies `Cyrus.json.settings` via the existing Palworld path. On Nxeon the ini
      is regenerated from env vars on every boot (`applyPalworld`, `REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES`), so a preset must either map
      to panel fields (`lib/game-config.ts` PALWORLD schema covers only ~10 keys) or switch the server to
      `raw-config-mode` and use `mergeOptionSettings` with the server STOPPED. Needs a design choice.
- [ ] Confirm destructive settings (bHardcore, bPalLost, bAutoResetGuildNoOnlinePlayers) get an explicit confirm step in the UI.
- [ ] End-to-end on a throwaway Nxeon Palworld server: apply a preset, restart, read the ini back, check in game.

**Before any Lua mod is offered for servers**
- [ ] Owner: decide whether Nxeon offers a Windows-under-Wine/Proton Palworld image (or trials `ue4ss-linux`). Without one,
      Lua mods are "for your own PC / a Windows server" only.
- [ ] Load-test sandbox (see below) and one real run per archetype; the post-hit hook's coverage and the data-table
      short names (`DT_ItemDataTable`, `DT_PalMonsterParameter`, `DT_PalDropItem`, `DT_PalWildSpawner`) are unrun.
- [ ] Read the real 1.0.5 revision off the title screen and set `PALWORLD_MIN_REVISION` (today Pocketpair's example 82182).

**Ongoing maintenance**
- [ ] Version table: bump `PALWORLD_CURRENT_VERSION` on every Palworld patch (1.0.0 Jul 10, 1.0.1 Jul 14, 1.0.2 Jul 28,
      1.0.2.1 Jul 30, 1.0.3 Aug 12, 1.0.4 Sep 7, 1.0.5 Sep 14 2026: every 1-4 weeks). Clients must match the server
      version, so old versions are "unsupported", and every mod gets the validator's "outdated" warning until rebuilt.
- [ ] Re-check the knowledge pack against a fresh PalworldModdingKit/header dump after each major patch.
- [ ] Watch: Steam app 2394010 build id, `Okaetsu/RE-UE4SS` experimental-palworld releases, `pocketpairjp/PalworldModUploader`, the server guide's config page.

## Verification harness assessment

Today: `static-lint` (the validator) plus the generated busted spec for pure logic (not run here: no Lua on node-2).
A real load test needs nothing proprietary to be redistributed, but it does need the game server:
1. A Windows (or Wine) sandbox with the free dedicated server via SteamCMD (`app_update 2394010`, anonymous login).
2. UE4SS Palworld build (MIT, `Okaetsu/RE-UE4SS` experimental-palworld, or the Workshop package) placed per the loader.
3. Drop the package into `Mods/Workshop/<id>/`, write `Mods/PalModSettings.ini`, start the server headless, wait for
   world load, then parse `UE4SS.log` for the mod's "loaded" line and any "unavailable in this game version" / Lua
   errors, then stop. ~10 GB disk, 8-16 GB RAM per run: it cannot run on node-2's 7 GB agent slice.
Not implemented (needs a Windows/Wine VM and owner sign-off). `verification.canRunSandbox` stays `false`.
A cheap middle step that IS possible: install `lua5.4` + `luacheck` + `busted` on the build host to compile-check every
generated file and run the generated specs (needs the owner's OK to add packages to node-2).

## Owner decisions
1. Ship server settings presets first? (recommended)
2. Preset install path on Nxeon: panel fields only, or raw-config mode + merge?
3. Windows/Wine Palworld image (or ue4ss-linux trial) for Lua server mods, yes/no?
4. OK to add Lua tooling (lua5.4/luacheck/busted) to node-2 for compile checks?

# How Palworld modding works (one page, also for the marketing page)

**Two very different things are called "Palworld mods".**

1. **Server settings.** Every Palworld server has a settings file (`PalWorldSettings.ini`) with about 100 switches and
   multipliers: XP rate, capture rate, how fast days and nights pass, how much pals and players hit, hunger, item
   weight, the death penalty, hardcore mode, raids, how many pals work at each base. Changing them needs no extra
   software, works on Linux and Windows servers, and **nobody who joins has to install anything**, including console
   players. This is what most server owners actually want ("double XP weekend", "hardcore rules").

2. **Script and content mods.** Palworld is an Unreal Engine 5.1 game. The community tool **UE4SS** lets mods run
   **Lua** scripts inside the game: they can hook the game's functions, read and change pals, items and data tables,
   and react to hits, spawns and time of day. Since v0.7 (Dec 2025) Palworld has an **official mod loader** and
   Steam Workshop support: a mod is a folder with an `Info.json` (name, package name, version, minimum game revision,
   dependencies and install rules) plus its files (`Scripts/` for Lua, `Paks/` for art and models, `LogicMods/` for
   Blueprint mods, `PalSchema/` for JSON data edits). Players switch mods on in the game's Mod Management menu.

- Mods marked for servers (`IsServer`) run on the **Windows** dedicated server only. Linux servers, which most hosts
  use, can't load them yet.
- Anything visual (new looks, overlays, UI, sounds) and anything the game predicts on the player's PC (movement
  speed) has to be installed by **every player**, on a **Windows PC**. Console, Mac and Game Pass can't use mods.
- Single-player and the host of a co-op world run everything locally, so most mods "just work" there.

**Why mods break.** Palworld updates every few weeks, players can only join a server on the exact same version, and a
patch can rename the internal names a script relies on. Pocketpair's guideline: mods are at your own risk, never use
them on official servers, back up saves first, and delete (not just disable) mod files before updating.

today) or an official-loader Lua package, and labels every mod with where it runs and whether players need it. It only
uses game names checked against Palworld's published headers, wraps every game call so a patch logs a warning instead
of crashing, keeps scripts out of save files, the network and your system, and flags mods as out of date when a new

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-game-palworld`. Palworld stays `status: "soon"`; going live is the owner's call.

## Verdict first: Linux vs Windows (confirmed from primary sources)

**Confirmed.** Pocketpair's own server guide says server-side mods work only on the **Windows** dedicated server
(https://docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/mod, fetched 2026-10-08). Their mod-loader docs list the
supported platforms as "Windows (Steam)" and "Windows dedicated server" only
(https://github.com/pocketpairjp/PalworldModUploader, `docs/en/01-General.md`). Nxeon's Palworld servers run the
native Linux server (`thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker`; config at `Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/`,
`lib/game-files-roots.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`). So:

| What | Works on Nxeon's Linux servers today? | Players install? |
|---|---|---|
| **Server settings presets** (`PalWorldSettings.ini`: XP, capture, day/night, death penalty, hardcore, base limits, raids...) | **Yes.** Every dedicated server, any OS. | No. Console / Mac / Game Pass players can join too. |
| UE4SS Lua mods via the official loader (`Info.json` + `IsServer` rule) | **No.** Windows dedicated server only. | Only if the mod also changes client-predicted things (movement) or visuals. |
| PalSchema JSON data mods (a UE4SS mod) | **No** (needs UE4SS; Windows only). | Server-side data changes: no. |
| LogicMods / Paks (Blueprint, textures, models, audio) | **No**; also need cooked UE 5.1 packages Cyrus can't produce. | **Yes**, every player. |
| Client-only Lua (overlays, post-process, key-bound abilities in single-player / co-op host) | n/a (runs on the player's Windows PC) | Yes, each player who wants it. |

Ways Lua could reach Nxeon later, both **unverified by Nxeon**: (a) run the Windows server under Wine/Proton in a
separate image (community images exist, e.g. `ripps818/docker-palworld-dedicated-server-wine`); (b) the community
Linux port `XarminaEu/ue4ss-linux` (MIT, verified by its author on Palworld 1.0.1, LD_PRELOAD; hooks need resolved
addresses on stripped binaries, no Blueprint loader, folders must be lowercase `scripts`, and the official loader does
not run there). **Cyrus therefore targets server settings presets first** for Nxeon customers, and labels every Lua mod
"can't be installed on Nxeon servers yet".

## What was built

- `lib/cyrus/games/palworld.ts`: verified `GameSupport` + `knowledge` pack (API sheet from Palworld's published headers
  and the UE4SS docs, 13 failure rules) + `PALWORLD_KINDS` (server-settings / server-lua / both-lua / host-lua / client-lua
  with customer-facing reasons).
- `lib/cyrus/games/palworld.settings.ts`: 70 documented settings with types and safety ranges, a blocked list
  (passwords, ports, RCON/REST, player cap...), `mergeOptionSettings` (pure merge into an existing ini; a partial
  OptionSettings line is NOT a patch), `settingsIntent` (plain words -> changes, zero API cost).
- `lib/cyrus/engine/games/palworld.ts` (generator v2): settings presets; Info.json packages; side-aware main.lua that
  starts on dedicated servers and PCs; all 17 `plausible:` names resolved (fixed or removed, list below); authority
  checks before every state change; data tables found by short name; file access confined to the mod folder.
- `lib/cyrus/games/palworld.validate.ts`: static validator (package format, side rules, Lua block/bracket structure,
  blocked APIs, MOD_DIR file rule, knowledge failure rules, verified-hook list, settings key checks).
- `test/cyrus-game-palworld.test.ts`: generator x validator across every category/model, settings, negative cases.

| Was | Now |
|---|---|
| `PalUtility:SendSystemAnnounce` | Verified (`PalUtility.h`), called with the world as context, server only |
| `StatusComponent:AddAdditionalEffect` | Does not exist. `StatusComponent:AddStatus(EPalStatusID)` |
| `PalTimeManager:GetCurrentDayTimeHour` | Does not exist. `UPalUtility:GetTimeManager():GetCurrentPalWorldTime_Hour()` + `UPalUtility:IsNight` |
| `PalDamageReactionComponent:ApplyDamageForMP` (pre-hook editing damage) | Does not exist. Post-hit hook on `CallOnActualDamageProcessed_ToAll` + bonus damage |
| `ShooterComponent:GetHasWeapon().ownItemId` | `GetHasWeapon():GetItemId().StaticId` (field is `ownItemID`) |
| `PalBaseCampModel.Transform / AreaRange` | Verified |
| `PalWorkProgress.CurrentWorkAmount / RequiredWorkAmount` | Verified |
| `CharacterParameterComponent:IsOtomo` | Verified |
| `player:GetRidingCharacter` | Does not exist. `UPalUtility:GetRidePal(player)` |
| `CharacterParameterComponent:GetWork` | Verified |
| `IndividualHandle.ID.InstanceId` | Verified |
| `DT_PalDropItem` CharacterID / ItemIdN / RateN | Verified (`FPalDropItemDatabaseRow`) |
| `PalSpawnerStandard.SpawnGroupList` | Not on any native class. Now `DT_PalWildSpawner` rows `LvMin_N/LvMax_N` (verified struct) |
| `PalPlayerState:EnterChat_Receive` | Does not exist. `PalPlayerState:EnterChat(FText)` |
| `AkGameplayStatics:PostEventByName` | Removed: no verified Wwise API; audio is a labelled template preview |
| Monster body `EmissiveColor` material param | Removed (unverifiable); variants keep lucky flag/rank/talents/scale |
| Bare `BeginDeferredActorSpawnFromClass` pal summon | Removed (breaks saves); "summon" effect staggers instead |

Also fixed (real bugs, not tagged): `SetHP` was called on the individual parameter (only the component has it);
`AddItem_ServerInternal` had 3 args (1.0 has 5); the mod never started on a dedicated server (ClientRestart +
IsLocalController only); `FindFirstOf("PalPlayerCharacter")` treated "first player" as "you".

**Can ship now (owner decision)**

- [ ] Read the real 1.0.5 revision off the title screen and set `PALWORLD_MIN_REVISION` (today Pocketpair's example 82182).

- [ ] Version table: bump `PALWORLD_CURRENT_VERSION` on every Palworld patch (1.0.0 Jul 10, 1.0.1 Jul 14, 1.0.2 Jul 28,

- [ ] Re-check the knowledge pack against a fresh PalworldModdingKit/header dump after each major patch.
- [ ] Watch: Steam app 2394010 build id, `Okaetsu/RE-UE4SS` experimental-palworld releases, `pocketpairjp/PalworldModUploader`, the server guide's config page.

## Verification harness assessment

Today: `static-lint` (the validator) plus the generated busted spec for pure logic (not run here: no Lua on node-2).
A real load test needs nothing proprietary to be redistributed, but it does need the game server:
1. A Windows (or Wine) sandbox with the free dedicated server via SteamCMD (`app_update 2394010`, anonymous login).
2. UE4SS Palworld build (MIT, `Okaetsu/RE-UE4SS` experimental-palworld, or the Workshop package) placed per the loader.
3. Drop the package into `Mods/Workshop/<id>/`, write `Mods/PalModSettings.ini`, start the server headless, wait for
   world load, then parse `UE4SS.log` for the mod's "loaded" line and any "unavailable in this game version" / Lua
   errors, then stop. ~10 GB disk, 8-16 GB RAM per run: it cannot run on node-2's 7 GB agent slice.
Not implemented (needs a Windows/Wine VM and owner sign-off). `verification.canRunSandbox` stays `false`.
A cheap middle step that IS possible: install `lua5.4` + `luacheck` + `busted` on the build host to compile-check every
generated file and run the generated specs (needs the owner's OK to add packages to node-2).

2. Preset install path on Nxeon: panel fields only, or raw-config mode + merge?
3. Windows/Wine Palworld image (or ue4ss-linux trial) for Lua server mods, yes/no?
4. OK to add Lua tooling (lua5.4/luacheck/busted) to node-2 for compile checks?

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

content.thinking:
The owner's Linux-only rule applies to server-side requirements, so I'm distinguishing that client-side Lua runs on the player's machine and isn't restricted the same way—Cyrus can still offer that as a clearly labeled client-side tip while refusing Windows-server-dependent mods.

I'm trying to map each refused request type to the nearest real settings knob: spawns to PalSpawnNumRate and EnemyDropItemRate increases, weapons to PlayerDamageRateAttack, but creature variants have no honest equivalent since Palworld's server settings can't generate rare variant creatures. For that case I'll have the generator produce a clear refusal with an explanation rather than force a fake alternative, while still outputting a Built response with a Cyrus.json marked "unsupported," a NOTES.md explaining why, and an alternative settings file when a genuine knob exists.

Simpler fix: add an optional refused field to the Cyrus.json schema capturing kind, reason, and alternative. When no alternative preset exists, output Cyrus.json with kind "unsupported" plus a NOTES.md, and have the validator treat "unsupported" as valid only if there are no scripts and no Info.json.

I need to add "unsupported" to the PalworldModKind union and corresponding PALWORLD_KINDS entry, marking it server-side, not Nxeon-compatible, labeled "Not supported on Nxeon". For install settings, since what actually works on Nxeon is server-side config (like the PalWorldSettings.ini path), I'm weighing whether to set side to "server" and realizing the existing packaging options don't really cover a plain ini file case.

I'll just use "zip" as the packaging type since none of the options truly fit a settings preset, flagging the mismatch in my reasoning for the coordinator. I'm setting hotReload to false and needsRestart to true since server settings require a restart, and adding a clientNote clarifying there's nothing to install server-side while client tips are optional and only apply to the player's own Windows PC — making sure I don't mark the game ready based on Windows-only client mods alone.

I'm reconsidering host-lua generation too: effects that depend on single-player/co-op hosting won't actually run on a dedicated Nxeon server, and the same goes for mods that alter authoritative game state like spells, items, companions, or quests — generating those for a Nxeon customer would be misleading since the client has no authority over the server. So I'll refuse host-lua and state-changing scripts, but keep client-lua elements like overlays, post-processing, or audio previews since those genuinely function as client-side-only tips.

I also need to update the test suite accordingly: the validator should now accept refusal outputs as valid responses for many categories, and I'll need to adjust the README install test and the creature-variant test to reflect refusals. I might also expose the Lua generation path behind an internal flag or export so it can still be tested directly, even though it's not surfaced to normal users.

I'll keep the raw Lua generator exported separately so tests can still reach it, while the actual build path enforces the Nxeon policy wrapper that restricts allowed Lua kinds to client-side only, mapping each setting category to its alternative config changes instead.

I need to restructure the build function to compute the mode first before deciding whether to produce a settings mod or an unsupported mod with refusal info, so I'll split it into a helper that returns both the built result and its mode.

| Server rules and balance: XP, capture, day/night length, pal and player damage, hunger, stamina, drops, gathering, work speed, egg hatch time, item weight, death penalty, PvP, hardcore, raids, fast travel, base and guild limits, randomizer, performance limits | **Builds a server settings preset** (`PalWorldSettings.ini`), checked against Pocketpair's documented keys with safe ranges | No (console players can join too) |
| Visual / interface tips: pal stats overlay, colour grade | **Builds a client-side tip**, labelled "client-side only: your own Windows PC, not your server" | Only the player who wants it |
| Anything needing a server script (spawn tables, rare variants, weapon retunes, base-job loops) | **Refuses**, says why (Palworld only loads server scripts on Windows), and offers the closest settings preset where an honest one exists (spawns -> spawn/drop rates, weapon -> player damage, worksite -> work speed, loot -> drop/gathering rates, partner regen -> pal HP regen) | n/a |
| Single-player / co-op-host scripts (spells, loot satchel, companion, expeditions, quests) and both-sides scripts (mount speed) | **Refuses**: the game ignores them on a dedicated server | n/a |
| New textures, models, sounds, Blueprint mods | **Refuses**: need cooked Unreal 5.1 packages on every player's PC | n/a |

The generator can still produce the other Lua kinds (`palworldLuaPackage`) and the validator lints them with
`{ nxeon: false }`, so nothing is lost if the policy ever changes, but `buildModFiles` (what customers get) never ships them.
Palworld must not be marked live on the strength of Windows-only mods; what is ready to consider is the settings preset path.

**Confirmed.** Pocketpair's own server guide says server-side mods work only on the **Windows** dedicated server
(https://docs.palworldgame.com/settings-and-operation/mod, fetched 2026-10-08). Their mod-loader docs list the
supported platforms as "Windows (Steam)" and "Windows dedicated server" only
(https://github.com/pocketpairjp/PalworldModUploader, `docs/en/01-General.md`). Nxeon's Palworld servers run the
native Linux server (`thijsvanloef/palworld-server-docker`; config at `Pal/Saved/Config/LinuxServer/`,
`lib/game-files-roots.ts`, `lib/game-control.ts`). So:

| What | Works on Nxeon's Linux servers today? | Players install? |
